name: Pnoepygidae
description: Cupwings are a family of small, secretive passerine birds found in the montane forests of southern and eastern Asia. They are named for their unique cup-shaped wings and are known for their skulking behavior.

children.name: Pnoepyga
children.description: A genus of tiny, almost tailless passerines with scaled underparts, inhabiting dense undergrowth in Asian forests.

children.name: Pnoepyga pusilla
children.description: The pygmy cupwing (Pnoepyga pusilla) or pygmy wren-babbler, is a species of bird in the Pnoepyga wren-babblers family, Pnoepygidae.

children.name: Pnoepyga immaculata
children.description: The Nepal cupwing (Pnoepyga immaculata), also known as the Nepal wren-babbler or immaculate cupwing, is a small species of passerine bird in the family Pnoepygidae.

children.name: Pnoepyga formosana
children.description: The Taiwan cupwing (Pnoepyga formosana), also known as Taiwan wren-babbler, is a species of passerine bird in the family Pnoepygidae.
